description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy of four different models as a function of the number of demonstrations on the 'BBQ' task. The x-axis is labeled '#Demonstrations', featuring a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1500 with tick labels spaced at intervals of 250 demonstrations. The y-axis is labeled 'Accuracy', using a linear scale from 45 to 55 with tick labels at intervals of 5. The 'Squared Exponential' model, represented by a solid dark blue line with circular markers, begins at approximately 52 accuracy at 0 demonstrations, rises steadily to 56 at 250 demonstrations, and then stabilizes near 56 for the remainder of the range. The 'Tanh' model, shown as a solid dark blue line with circular markers, starts at about 48 accuracy and exhibits a slight decline to 47 at 1500 demonstrations. The 'ELU' model, depicted as a solid dark blue line with circular markers, begins at 46 accuracy and shows a gradual increase to 48 at 1500 demonstrations. The 'LLmA-2-chat-7B' model, indicated by a dashed pink line with circular markers, maintains a constant accuracy of 43 across all demonstration points.
caption_used: The line plot illustrates the accuracy of different models as a function of the number of demonstrations, providing a comparison of performance trends on the 'BBQ' task. The x-axis is labeled '#Demonstrations', with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1500 and tick labels at intervals of 250 demonstrations. The y-axis is labeled 'Accuracy', with a linear scale ranging from 45 to 55, and tick labels at intervals of 5. The 'Squared Exponential' model starts at an accuracy of approximately 52 at 0 demonstrations, increases steadily to 56 at 250 demonstrations, and then stabilizes. The 'Tanh' model begins at about 48 accuracy at 0 demonstrations and shows a slight decline to 47 at 1500 demonstrations. The 'ELU' model starts at 46 accuracy and shows a gradual increase to 48 at 1500 demonstrations. The 'LLmA-2-chat-7B' model maintains a consistent accuracy of 43 across all demonstration points, performing significantly worse than the other models. The 'Squared Exponential' model consistently outperforms all other models, with the 'ELU' model showing the second-best performance overall.
